minutes.headline: Zoning Board failed to reach the four votes needed on a Gilchrist Street seven-lot special permit; the vote was confused.
minutes.summary: The board heard a continued petition for a special permit for dimensional variation on seven lots at Gilchrist Street and Valley Road, tied to a land swap with the town. The engineer for the applicant presented, abutters raised concerns about precedent, driveways, septic and traffic, and members questioned whether the bylaw allows this for new lots. A motion to deny drew a split and confusing count, and a motion to approve also did not reach the needed supermajority; the chair then said the plan was denied.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals did not reach the four votes needed for the Gilchrist Street and Valley Road seven-lot special permit, and the chair declared the plan denied.
A motion to approve the plan as presented got three in favor and two against, short of the four-vote supermajority, so it did not pass.
A motion to deny, on the ground that the plan goes against the intent of the bylaw, drew a confused count; the chair first said it did not carry, then said the plan was denied.
Abutters raised septic, driveway, traffic and precedent concerns about the seven lots, which are tied to a land swap with the town; one speaker supported the plan.
The board said it would submit names the next day to seat a full regular member on the Zoning Board.

why_it_matters: The result decides whether seven new house lots can be built near Gilchrist Street and Valley Road, and whether the related land swap with the town goes ahead as proposed.
The confused count and the supermajority rule leave the outcome open to question, and the board's shortage of full regular members affected how close the vote was.
